1: Looking up which plugins are enabled and where their settings come from should work whether or not the Claude setup folders already exist. Instead, on a fresh or partly set-up machine the lookup often crashes with a file-not-found error, and when the Claude command-line tool is missing, broken, or returns bad output, no clear problem is reported. Malformed plugin catalogs and unreadable settings also go unflagged, so the user sees an incomplete plugin list with no warning.
2: When the Claude command-line tool reports an error while listing plugins or marketplaces, the user should see a clean, readable message saying what went wrong. Instead, the message shows raw byte-string formatting with quotation marks and a b prefix, and some locally installed plugins are missing from the listing even though they are present.
3: When the Claude command-line tool succeeds, the listing should come back as normal information, not as an error. Instead, the tool reports a failure that echoes the marketplace data back as the error text, and when the tool does fail, the message wrongly says the output could not be read. Plugin status also disagrees between checks: a plugin that is enabled or synced can be shown as inactive or not installed in one place and active in another.
4: Asking which plugins are installed should return what the Claude command-line tool reports, and a plugin that is enabled and synced should show as active. Instead, the plugin list often comes back empty regardless of what is installed, enabled and synced plugins are shown as inactive or as not fully synced, and a broken tool response goes through without any error being raised.
5: Looking up the skills a user has should list their personal skills and the skills from each plugin, and a missing skills folder should simply mean there are no skills. Instead, the lookup crashes when the skills folder is missing, a personal skill the user has hidden still shows as active, and a skill name without a plugin prefix is attributed to the wrong place.
6: Reading the drift report should show which skills keep going wrong, and an empty or missing history should give an empty report rather than an error. Instead, nearly every run of the report crashes with an index error, including when no history exists, so the patterns, the owner of each skill, and the file it names cannot be shown at all.
7: The drift summary command should print every open problem grouped by skill with its counts, and the drift command should show the same view. Instead, asking for the summary is rejected as an unknown command, and the entries show the corrected and deviated counts swapped, so the report misstates how often each kind of problem happened.
8: Recording a problem against a skill should count only the latest version of that skill, and a saved record should read back with the same details it was saved with. Instead, earlier versions are still counted in the totals, saved records cannot be read back whole, and numeric settings are accepted or rejected inconsistently, so the totals across sessions come out wrong.
9: Marking one or more problems as reviewed should remove them from the open list, and the open list should keep every problem on a skill that is still active. Instead, marking problems does not take effect as expected, active skills are dropped from the open list, retired skills stay in the counts, and the totals shown do not match the actual number of open problems.
10: Loading the accumulated drift records should return the log, the grouped problems, and the list of retired skills together, and problems the user has marked as reviewed should stay gone in later runs. Instead, the load crashes when there are no records to read, and marked problems are not remembered, so already-reviewed problems reappear in every later run.
